principles: Metadata mirrors runtime: register the gate on exactly the lifecycle transitions that correspond to the 4 runtime START->DEV doors — never invent or omit a door.
No behavior change: touch only descriptive registries + the drift check + docs; machine.ts stays frozen.
Extend the single existing drift source (verify-process-fact-contract.mjs) rather than add a parallel test surface.
Match existing shapes: reuse the kebab-case gate-id convention and the existing consumer-registration form.
drivers: the metadata must match the live machine.ts gate exactly
the drift check must mechanically protect the gate going forward

options.name: register-and-extend-check
cons: must precisely map lifecycle transitions to runtime doors

options.name: doc-note-only
cons: leaves the machine-readable registries stale; the drift check still cannot catch future divergence — does not actually close the gap

rationale: Registering the parallel-decomposition gate id on the lifecycle DEV-entry transitions that map to the 4 runtime doors + adding the process-fact consumer + extending verify-process-fact-contract.mjs to assert the guard surface makes the descriptive contract match the live machine.ts gate AND mechanically guards against future drift, all without touching runtime. A doc-note-only approach would leave the machine-readable registries stale and the drift check blind.

preMortem.scenario: The gate is registered on a lifecycle transition that is NOT actually a runtime door (or omitted from one that IS), so the metadata lies about enforcement
preMortem.trigger: the 6+ to:DEV lifecycle entries are not carefully mapped to the 4 runtime START->DEV doors (canStartDev/canSkipPlan/canReenterDev)
preMortem.consequence: audits/projections report the wrong door coverage — the exact drift this story exists to fix, now inverted
preMortem.mitigation: in DEV, read each to:DEV transition source phase + event and cross-check against machine.ts guards; register on EXACTLY the INIT_CHECK/PLAN/REVIEW/TEST START->DEV doors; the extended drift check asserts the mapping

preMortem.scenario: The change accidentally alters runtime gating (e.g. a gate id that is actually consumed for enforcement, not just description)
preMortem.trigger: assuming .gates is purely descriptive when some consumer reads it to enforce
preMortem.consequence: a metadata-only chore silently changes PLAN->DEV behavior
preMortem.mitigation: S5 review already established .gates is descriptive (enforcement is the xstate guards); re-confirm no enforcement path reads the new gate id; lattice validate + the integration smoke (unchanged) stay green proving runtime behavior is unchanged

preMortem.scenario: verify-process-fact-contract.mjs is extended in a way that passes vacuously (asserts nothing real) or breaks the existing check
preMortem.trigger: a tautological assertion or one that does not actually read the new registration
preMortem.consequence: the drift check gives false confidence and will not catch a future regression
preMortem.mitigation: the new assertion must read the actual registration and FAIL if the parallel gate is removed from the metadata; verify by temporarily removing the registration and confirming the check fails, then restore
